verdict.rationale: Hatchet's architecture separates a central control plane that coordinates worker execution from the workers themselves, which run independently as part of the user's application. Paid hosted tiers on the pricing page suggest a vendor-managed control plane, so workers in your own infrastructure with code staying local is implied, though not stated as a documented hybrid mode. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a managed-cloud control plane connecting to customer-hosted workers, any evidence that task payloads/data stay inside the customer network, network/connectivity requirements for remote workers, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I run workers in my own infrastructure while the vendor manages the orchestration control plane — code and data stay inside my network

citations.quote: the Hatchet Control Plane - the central orchestration system that manages workflows, schedules tasks, and coordinates worker execution.
Hatchet is a separate service which runs independently of your workers
When you’re ready to scale, upgrade anytime and only pay for what you use.
